content.intro: Learn signals and event-driven hooks through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Signals and Event-Driven Hooks matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines signals and event-driven hooks as part of advanced django architecture. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Model signals; Request signals; Signal receivers; Signal registration; When explicit function calls are easier to reason about. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Model signals
items.text: Signals allow decoupled listeners but can hide control flow. Use them for genuinely cross-cutting hooks, register receivers predictably, and consider a direct function call for core business steps.
